text: On 10 September 2025, the Paris Court of Appeal found that an employee's stalled career and pay at Société Générale resulted from discrimination linked to her sex and her origins; the ruling is reported as the court's first recognition of 'intersectional discrimination'.
short: 2025 Paris appeal-court finding: Société Générale discriminated against an employee on sex and origin

source.name: France-Guyane: Discriminée parce que femme et noire — la Société Générale condamnée
source.quote: Le 10 septembre 2025, la cour d'appel de Paris a reconnu que la stagnation professionnelle et salariale de Maeva(1) résultait d'une discrimination liée à son genre et à ses origines.
source.note: English: 'On 10 September 2025, the Paris Court of Appeal recognised that the professional and pay stagnation of Maeva resulted from discrimination linked to her gender and her origins. A first.'

additionalSources.name: StreetPress: À la Société Générale, une affaire de discrimination raciale balayée par les prud’hommes
additionalSources.quote: la Cour d’appel de Paris condamnait la Société Générale pour discrimination « en raison de l’origine et du sexe »
additionalSources.note: English: 'the Paris Court of Appeal convicted Société Générale of discrimination on grounds of origin and sex' — another employee of the bank. StreetPress links the Mediapart report (paywalled).
